title: Certify infinite-order growth of swapped source-code charts
body:
## Summary

```text
research/source-code-chart-order/
  README.md       three-section proof and scope
  verify.py       pinned-source extraction and exact replay
  test_verify.py  literal results and CLI failure controls
  *.json          receipt, source pins, task and replay manifest
```

Prove a concrete changing-chart obstruction on the selected 112-port query matrix. PR1862's two admissible charts, with compensation/query sets A and T swapped, each have order six. Their alternating source-only product has infinite order, with characteristic polynomial

`(t-1)^88 (t^3-171t^2+27t-1)^8`.

Its trace is 1456 and a real eigenvalue lies strictly between 170 and 171. No positive number of repetitions restores every source. This quantifies PR1862's existing warning; it does not dispute its valid fixed-chart construction.

Started from main `d48fcf5eedae9d8e2296598a1868a0b1a37a83f1`. The catalogue proposed `complex-new-helper-inventory`; TASK.json declares the change to a source-restoration audit, not a new inventory or exponent improvement. [Discussion #1976](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1976) records coordination.

## Evidence

- Before, the known fixed-chart code has order six. The same-chart pair returns after three repetitions, retained as a positive control.
- After swapping charts, a source-bound 24-dimensional section calculation yields the cubic above. Exact integer signs at 170 and 171 are -24311 and 4616. A separate ordered-factor interpreter agrees on all 336 individual/product source-column cases.
- Eight focused tests pass in standard and optimized execution, including four semantic controls, a corrupted archive, a forged receipt and CLI failures.
- The unchanged registered launcher passes in standard and optimized modes on Linux, CPython 3.12.15. Each replay includes the source pins, 336 column comparisons, four semantic controls and all eight focused tests.
- Package metadata/Git/SHA256 pins, `-Wall` compilation and diff checks pass. All 45 research-workflow tests pass under 3.12 with no skips. The earlier CPython 3.13.5 direct replays also passed; its workflow run had two version-gated skips.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/source-code-chart-order
python3.12 -I -O -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/source-code-chart-order
python3.12 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'
```

Installed CPython 3.12.15 in an isolated user directory from Astral's SHA256-verified standalone release. The default Python 3.13.5 is unchanged. README.md and TASK.json now record the completed registered replay and interpreter provenance. No verifier, test, manifest, source pin, exact receipt or shared version check changed. Full selected cold replay, native routing, hosting/precision admission and proof-assistant verification are not claimed.

Credit Ali Romman / PR1862 for the source code and changing-chart warning, and David Arias / PR1973 for fixed-code controller winding and the different F-B-F defect. This contribution instead determines the repeated source-only swapped-chart product's polynomial and growth. Exact predecessor heads are in TASK.json. Jeremy Kothe, Rohan Arun and the retained selected-supplier lineage keep their credit; all frozen inputs and notices remain intact.

Final overlap refresh covered 610 Discussion records and a separately paginated 468 live open PRs. The stock helper's PR refresh cannot use this host's older `gh --slurp`; live REST pages covered that gap. No global novelty claim is made.

## Merge danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: research.

Only the new package changes. No selected frontier, existing verifier, frozen source, supplier invoice or global controller changes. The theorem concerns this source-only pair, not all chart sequences or native transports. The next question is to derive and price an actual transport that restores the full source rather than only its query.
